# Endpoints and JSON

A `.ts` file with no template of the same name is an **endpoint**: it serves its own URL from code. Use one for JSON, feeds, webhooks, event streams and anything else that isn't an HTML page.

```ts
// pb_pages/feeds/latest.ts
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20)
    return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) => ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') })))
  },
}
```

A request to `/feeds/latest` returns:

```json
[{ "id": "abc123", "title": "Hello" }]
```

## How it works

- The URL comes from the file's path, as for pages: `feeds/latest.ts` serves `/feeds/latest`, `feeds/index.ts` serves `/feeds`, `products/[id].ts` serves `/products/123`.
- An endpoint has the same exports as [page code](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data#page-code): `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`.
- There is no template, so a handler must send a response. Returning without one is a `500`.
- A method with no handler answers `405`, `GET` included, with an `Allow` header listing the methods it has.
- An endpoint and a page can't claim the same URL: `feed.ts` and `feed/index.ets` is an error at startup.
- Middleware runs for endpoints too; layouts don't.
- Handlers can be `async`. The response is sent once the handler settles.

## Errors

An error thrown in an endpoint (`ctx.httpError()` or any other) answers with JSON: `{ "status": 404, "message": "..." }`. When the request's `Accept` header puts `text/html` first, as a browser does when someone opens the URL, the error is your `+error.ets` page instead.

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id].ts
module.exports = {
  get(ctx) {
    const product = ctx.app.findFirstRecordByFilter('products', 'id = {:id}', { id: ctx.params.id })
    if (!product) throw ctx.httpError(404, 'No such product')
    return ctx.res.json({ id: product.id, name: product.getString('name') })
  },
}
```

## Async handlers

```ts
// pb_pages/stats.ts
module.exports = {
  async get(ctx) {
    const orders = await ctx.app.countRecords.async('orders')
    return ctx.res.json({ orders })
  },
}
```

An async handler still has to send a response. Returning a value without calling `ctx.res.json` (or another
`ctx.res` method) is a `500`, as it is for a sync handler.

## Sending responses

| Call | Sends |
|---|---|
| `ctx.res.json(data)` / `ctx.res.json(status, data)` | JSON |
| `ctx.res.text(text)` / `ctx.res.text(status, text)` | Plain text |
| `ctx.res.html(html)` / `ctx.res.html(status, html)` | HTML as-is, without layouts |
| `ctx.res.file(path)` | A file from `pb_pages` |
| `ctx.res.redirect(location)` | A redirect |
| `ctx.res.sse()` | A `text/event-stream` |

See [res](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res).

## JSON from a page

JSON is only sent through `ctx.res.json` (and an endpoint's errors). Template output is never parsed as JSON, even if it looks like JSON. A page's code can still answer with JSON for one method:

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id].ts, beside products/[id].ets
module.exports = {
  post(ctx) {
    const product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id)
    return ctx.res.json({ id: product.id, name: product.getString('name') })
  },
}
```

## Keep `/api/` free

`/api/` belongs to PocketBase. Pages never see it, and a `pb_pages/api/` folder is an error at startup. Put your endpoints somewhere else, such as `feeds/`, `xapi/` or `hooks/`.
